premises: Hierarchical heterostructure features (interface density, chemical fluctuation amplitude) can be quantified and used as descriptors.
These microstructural descriptors, combined with CALPHAD parameters, can predict Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture toughness.
A hybrid ML model trained on a modest dataset can achieve ±10–15% prediction error for these properties.
The hybrid model reduces computational cost by an order of magnitude over full first-principles/CALPHAD.
Fracture toughness of HfNbTiVAl10 can be reliably predicted by this data-driven approach.
